# Module objectives

At the end of this module, you should be able to:

- use RStudio to write and run R code in the console and in scripts;
- install and load packages;
- create and manipulate R objects;
- use conditions and existing functions;
- write a simple function;
- apply a few tidyverse style conventions;
- check whether a dataset contains missing values;
- extract a row or column, add a column and filter data;
- write a simple Quarto report with text, code and sections.

# Initial readings

## Reference book

In this course, we will regularly rely on R for Data Science, 2nd edition, by Hadley Wickham, Mine Çetinkaya-Rundel and Garrett Grolemund.

We will often abbreviate this book as R4DS. It is freely available online and provides concrete examples for learning to work effectively with R and the tidyverse.

If you are stuck, also consult [How to search and get help](../references.qmd).

## Essential readings

- [R4DS homepage](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/){target="_blank"}
  Overview of the book, its authors and the general progression.

- [Introduction](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/intro.html){target="_blank"}
  Why learn R for data science and how to approach this course.

- [Workflow: basics](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/workflow-basics.html){target="_blank"}
  First practical moves in RStudio, the console, scripts and objects.

- [Workflow: scripts and projects](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/workflow-scripts.html){target="_blank"}
  Why keeping code in files makes work reproducible.

## Readings for the adventure and challenge

- [Hello, Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/hello/rstudio.html){target="_blank"}
  Create a first Quarto document, insert code and produce HTML output.

- [Data transformation](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/data-transform.html){target="_blank"}
  Introduction to `dplyr`, with verbs for filtering, choosing columns and creating variables.

## Posit cheat sheets

- [RStudio IDE :: Cheatsheet](https://rstudio.github.io/cheatsheets/rstudio-ide.pdf){target="_blank"}
  Quick reference for the RStudio environment.

- [Publish and Share with Quarto :: Cheatsheet](https://rstudio.github.io/cheatsheets/quarto.pdf){target="_blank"}
  Short reference for creating, rendering and sharing Quarto documents.

- [Data transformation with dplyr :: Cheatsheet](https://rstudio.github.io/cheatsheets/data-transformation.pdf){target="_blank"}
  `dplyr` verbs used in the first table manipulations.

## Reading mini-test

After the essential readings, complete the [module 1 formative mini-test](mini_test.qmd). It is not graded, but it checks points that return in the adventure and in the challenge.

# Adventure

This module places you in the role of a beginning analyst. You prepare the foundations of a first reproducible report with R, RStudio and Quarto, using `UlavalSSD::MeteoQuebec`.

[Module 1 adventure](aventure.qmd)

# Challenge

In this first challenge, you create a Quarto report in HTML format. The report answers a simple question using `MeteoQuebec`: compare the mean temperature observed on a chosen date across several years.

[Module 1 challenge](defi.qmd)

# Further reading

## Deepen best practices

- [Workflow: help](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/workflow-help.html){target="_blank"}
  Search documentation effectively and formulate a useful request for help.

- [Quarto formats](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/quarto-formats.html){target="_blank"}
  Understand possible Quarto formats and output options.

- [Workflow: style](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/workflow-style.html){target="_blank"}
  Why consistent code style supports reading, collaboration and feedback.

## Tidyverse style guide

- [Files](https://style.tidyverse.org/files.html){target="_blank"}
  Organize files, name scripts and structure a project.

- [Syntax](https://style.tidyverse.org/syntax.html){target="_blank"}
  Write readable code with clear and regular syntax.

# Consolidation exercises

Exercises are grouped on a standalone page. They consolidate module techniques and are not a step in the challenge.

[Module 1 exercises](exercices.qmd)

The series includes exercises on RStudio, objects, missing values, style, Quarto, `MeteoQuebec` and two final case studies with small fictitious files.
